rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet calls Yā Sīn the Qurʾān’s heart and promises forgiveness and reward like reciting the Qurʾān twenty-two times for reciting it sincerely.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 943 ) ( إن لكل شيء قلبا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A second report attributed to the Prophet says Yā Sīn intercedes for its reciter and brings forgiveness to its listener; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( 944 ) ( إن في القرآن سورة يشفع قارئها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following Sūrat al-Ṣāffāt is Meccan; it is counted as 181 verses, with 182 also reported.
rows.anchor: مكية ، وهي مائة وإحدى وثمانون آية ، وقيل : واثنتان وثمانون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed poetic citation uses استناص for striving to escape from a handler, apparently witnessing the adjacent verse’s related word for escape, مناص.
rows.anchor: غمر الجراء إذا قصرت عنانه … بيدي استناص ورام جري المسحل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent down is rain.
rows.anchor: هو المطر . وقيل : كل ماء في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative view says all water on earth comes from the sky, descending to a rock before God apportions it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : كل ماء في الأرض فهو من السماء ينزل منها إلى الصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means that God inserts and orders the water into springs and into channels and courses through the earth, like veins in bodies.
rows.anchor: فأدخله ونظمه { ينابيع فى الارض } عيونا ومسالك ومجاري كالعروق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The differing colors include the plants’ forms and hues, such as green, red, yellow, and white, as well as crop varieties such as wheat, barley, and sesame.
rows.anchor: هيئاته من خضرة وحمرة وصفرة وبياض وغير ذلك ، وأصنافه من بر وشعير

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī glosses يهيج as completing its drying: then the crop is ready to rise from its roots and disappear.
rows.anchor: عن الأصمعي ؛ لأنه إذا تم جفافه حان له أن يثور عن منابته ويذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حطاما means fragments and dry plant debris.
rows.anchor: فتاتا ودرينا { إن فى ذلك لذكرى } لتذكيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing crop reminds people that a wise maker exists and that creation follows determination and management, rather than idleness or neglect.
rows.anchor: لتذكيرا وتنبيها ، على أنه لا بد من صانع حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The crop’s cycle may also stand as a likeness for worldly life, as in the examples at 10:24 and 18:45.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مثلا للدنيا ، كقوله تعالى : { إنما مثل الحيواة الدنيا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read مصفارا.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( مصفارا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows who is fit for لطف and grants it, so that the person’s breast opens to Islam, welcomes it, and accepts it; one without this لطف remains constricted and hard-hearted.
rows.anchor: عرف الله أنه من أهل اللطف فلطف به حتى انشرح صدره للإسرم ورغب فيه وقبله كمن لا لطف له فهو حرج الصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light from his Lord is God’s لطف.
rows.anchor: ونور الله : هو لطفه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After reciting the verse, the Prophet says the heart opens and expands when light enters it; its sign is turning toward the eternal home, leaving worldly delusion, and preparing for death.
rows.anchor: وقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question omits its predicate, as does the construction in 39:9.
rows.anchor: في حذف الخبر { من ذكر الله } من أجل ذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here من means because of remembrance: when God or His signs are mentioned to the hard-hearted, they recoil and grow still more hardened, like those addressed in 9:125.
rows.anchor: من أجل ذكره ، أي : إذا ذكر الله عندهم أو آياته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads عن ذكر الله.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( عن ذكر الله ) فإن قلت : ما الفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With من, hardness arises because of remembrance; with عن, the heart is too hardened and estranged to accept remembrance. He illustrates the contrast with giving water because of thirst versus giving it until thirst is gone.
rows.anchor: قسا قلبه من ذكر الله ، فالمعنى ما ذكرت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that the Companions tired of the same routine and asked the Prophet to tell them something; this verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه : أن أصحاب رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making God the subject and predicating نزّل of Him magnifies the best discourse, confirms its divine source, and signals its miraculous distinction from ordinary speech.
rows.anchor: وإيقاع اسم الله مبتدأ وبناء { نزل } عليه : فيه تفخيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كتابا can be an appositive replacing أحسن الحديث.
rows.anchor: بدل من أحسن الحديث . ويحتمل أن يكون حالا منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, كتابا is a circumstantial accusative describing أحسن الحديث.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون حالا منه { متشابها } مطلق في مشابهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qurʾān’s parts resemble one another in soundness, firmness, truth, benefit, apt wording, precise expression, and the mutually reinforcing, inimitable structure of its composition.
rows.anchor: في الصحة والإحكام ، والبناء على الحق والصدق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مثاني may explain how the book is متشابها, since its repeated stories resemble one another; مثاني is the plural of مثنى, meaning repeated.
rows.anchor: لأن القصص المكررة لا تكون إلا متشابهة . والمثاني : جمع مثنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called repeated because its stories, accounts, rulings, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, and admonitions recur.
rows.anchor: ولما ثنى من قصصه وأنبائه ، وأحكامه ، وأوامره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the Qurʾān is repeatedly recited and does not grow dull or stale through frequent repetition.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأنه يثني في التلاوة ، فلا يمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further derivation takes مثاني as a repeated or doubled form, like كرتين at 67:4, meaning one return after another, and paired expressions such as لبيك سعديك.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع مثنى مفعل ، من التثنية بمعنى التكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A singular book may take a plural description because it is a whole consisting of detailed parts; the author compares this to the Qurʾān’s divisions and to a human made of bones, veins, and nerves.
rows.anchor: إنما صح ذلك لأن الكتاب جملة ذات تفاصيل ، وتفاصيل الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible underlying construction supplies فصولا: a book resembling one another in its sections, which are repeated.
rows.anchor: وأصله : كتابا متشابها فصولا مثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the plural form works as a descriptive predicate like برمة أعشار or ثوب أخلاق.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون كقولك : برمة أعشار ، وثوب أخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, مثاني is not an adjective but a distinguishing accusative after متشابها, meaning its aspects or qualities are repeated, like رجل حسن شمائل.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن لا يكون مثاني صفة ، ويكون منتصبا على التمييز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition is needed because people resist admonition; returning to it repeatedly helps it take root in them.
rows.anchor: النفوس أنفر شيء من حديث الوعظ والنصيحة ، فما لم يكرر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet’s custom was to repeat admonition three or seven times so it would take root in people’s hearts.
rows.anchor: عادة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يكرر عليهم ما كان يغط به وينصح ثلاث مرات وسبعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اقشعر describes intense contraction; its root evokes dry leather, with an added ر producing a quadriliteral form and an added sense of intensity.
rows.anchor: اقشعر الجلد : إذا تقبض تقبضا شديدا ، وتركيبه من حروف القشع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is an image for intense fear, when the skin tightens and its hairs stand on end.
rows.anchor: اقشعر جلده من الخوف وقف شعره ، وهو مثل في شدة الخوف

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bodily reaction may be figurative, portraying the extremity of their awe, or literal: Qurʾānic warnings make their skin shiver, then recollection of God’s mercy softens skin and hearts.
rows.anchor: فيجوز أن يريد به الله سبحانه التمثيل ، تصويرا لإفراط خشيتهم

words: تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: تلين is construed with إلى by incorporating the sense of a verb that takes إلى, such as becoming still or tranquil toward something.
rows.anchor: ضمن معنى فعل متعد بإلى ، كأنه قيل : سكنت . أو اطمأنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse names God rather than mercy because mercy and compassion are fundamental to His way, and His mercy precedes His anger.
rows.anchor: لأن أصل أمره الرحمة والرأفة ، ورحمته هي سابقة غضبه

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He first mentions skin alone because fear’s location in the heart is already implicit; at the outset hearts fear and skin shivers, then remembrance replaces fear with hope and shivering with softness.
rows.anchor: إذا ذكرت الخشية التي محلها القلوب ، فقد ذكرت القلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك points to the book: God guides His pious servants through it so they fear Him and hope in His mercy.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الكتاب ، وهو { هدى الله يهدى به } يوفق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ذلك refers to the described fear and hope as the effect of God’s لطف, called guidance because it results from guidance.
rows.anchor: أو ذلك الكائن من الخشية والرجاء هدي الله ، أي : أثر هداه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative reading, others who see the fearful and hopeful people may be drawn to imitate their conduct and path.
rows.anchor: من صحب أولئك ورآهم خاشين راجين ، فكان ذلك مرغبا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s leading astray means withholding لطف from transgressors and wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: من الفساق والفجرة { فما له من هاد }

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God’s لطف has no effect on those whose hard hearts and persistence in wickedness leave them beyond influence or guidance.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يؤثر فيه ألطافه لقسوة قلبه وإصراره على فجوره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What appears from God is a terrifying threat: a measure of His wrath and punishment they had never imagined or anticipated, like the concealed promise at 32:17.
rows.anchor: { وبدا لهم من الله } وعيد لهم لا كنه لفظاعته وشدته ، وهو نظير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, people considered their deeds good but discover that they are evil.
rows.anchor: وقيل : عملوا أعمالا حسبوها حسنات ، فإذا هي سيئات

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: Al-Thawrī recited the verse and twice lamented that it boded ill for people who act for show.
rows.anchor: وعن سفيان الثوري أنه قرأها فقال : ويل لأهل الرياء

rows.speaker: محمد بن المنكدر
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munkadir feared this verse as he was dying, worrying that God might reveal a punishment he had not reckoned with.
rows.anchor: وجزع محمد بن المنكدر عند موته فقيل له ، فقال : أخشى آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean the evil deeds they acquired, which were hidden from them until their records were displayed, as in 58:6.
rows.anchor: أي سيئات أعمالهم التي كسبوها . أو سيئات كسبهم ، حين تعرض صحائفهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, سيئات names the varieties of punishment they receive for what they earned, as in 42:40.
rows.anchor: وأراد بالسيئات : أنواع العذاب التي يجازون بها على ما كسبوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حاق means that the recompense for their mockery came down on them and surrounded them.
rows.anchor: ونزل بهم وأحاط جزاء هزئهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhwīl is exclusively a favor: خولني means giving someone something without compensation.
rows.anchor: التخويل : مختص بالتفضل . ويقال : خولني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One possible claim is that the recipient knew he would be given this because of his merit and entitlement.
rows.anchor: على علم مني أني سأعطاه ، لما في من فضل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the speaker means God knows him and knows he deserves the gift.
rows.anchor: أو على علم من الله بي وباستحقاقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third possibility is that the speaker attributes the gift to his own knowledge of how to earn wealth, like Qarun’s boast in 28:78.
rows.anchor: على علم مني بوجوه الكسب ، كما قال قارون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine pronoun in أوتيته treats نعمة as a thing or portion of blessings in sense; alternatively, ما in إنما is a relative pronoun to which it refers.
rows.anchor: ذهابا به إلى المعنى ؛ لأن قوله : { نعمة منا } شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply rejects the claim: the gift is instead a test of whether its recipient will be grateful or ungrateful.
rows.anchor: إنكار لقوله كأنه قال : ما خولناك من خولناك من النعمة

words: إنما أوتيته على علم بل هى فتنة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun shifts from masculine to feminine first by meaning and then by the wording فتنة; a feminine predicate licenses the feminine subject, as in ما جاءت حاجتك.
rows.anchor: حملا على المعنى أولا ، وعلى اللفظ آخرا ؛ ولأن الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads بل هو فتنة, matching the masculine construction of إنما أوتيته.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( بل هو فتنة ) وفق { إنما أوتيته }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ف here connects the distress prayer to the earlier recoil from God’s mention and delight in mentioning idols at 39:45; the intervening verses are an aside that reinforces the rebuke, unlike the parallel opening passage at 39:8, which is simply coordinated with what precedes.
rows.anchor: السبب في ذلك أن هذه وقعت مسببة عن قوله : { وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although disgust at God would seem to prompt avoidance, the ف treats the disbeliever’s appeal in hardship as if his denial caused the same appeal that faith causes, thereby exposing and censuring his inconsistency.
rows.anchor: في هذه التسبيب لطف ، وبيانه أن تقول : زيد مؤمن بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subsequent prayer in 39:46 and threat in 39:47 further underscore the rejection of those who recoil from God yet turn to Him in hardship; the same sequence is contrasted with the earlier passage at 39:8.
rows.anchor: ثم ما عقبه من الوعيد العظيم : تأكيد لإنكار اشمئزازهم واستبشارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in قالها refers to the earlier statement إنما أوتيته على علم at 28:78 and 39:49, since it is a word or sentence.
rows.anchor: راجع إلى قوله : { إنما أوتيته على علم } ( القصص : 78 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads قاله, using the masculine pronoun to refer to قول or كلام.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( قد قاله ) على معنى القول والكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier speakers were Qarun and his people: he said this and they approved it, so the statement is attributed to them all.
rows.anchor: والذين من قبلهم : هم قارون وقومه ، حيث قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, other people in earlier nations made the same claim.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون في الأمم الخالية آخرون قائلون مثلها

words: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly goods and wealth those earlier people acquired did not avail them.
rows.anchor: من متاع الدنيا ويجمعون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هؤلاء refers to the Meccan polytheists; their leaders were killed at Badr and they lost provision in a seven-year drought, before rain and abundance came for seven years.
rows.anchor: من مشركي قومك { سيصيبهم } مثل ما أصاب أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lesson is that God alone withholds or expands provision.
rows.anchor: فقيل لهم : { أو لم * يعلموا } أنه لا قابض ولا باسط إلا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Light here is borrowed for truth and revelation: the earth shines through the truth and justice God establishes in judgment and in weighing good and evil deeds.
rows.anchor: قد استعار الله عز وجل النور للحق والقرآن والبرهان في مواضع من التنزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is attributed to God because He is truth and justice, and the earth is attributed to Him because His justice adorns it; justice makes a land most beautiful and flourishing.
rows.anchor: وينادي عليه بأنه مستعار إضافته إلى اسمه ؛ لأنه هو الحق العدل . وإضافة اسمه إلى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following placement of the record, arrival of prophets and witnesses, and judgment in truth constitute the light just described; people likewise say a just ruler brightens the world with justice.
rows.anchor: ثم ما عطف على إشراق الأرض من وضع الكتاب والمجيء بالنبيين والشهداء والقضاء بالحق وهو النور المذكور

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that injustice is darknesses on the Day of Resurrection; the author links the verse’s opening affirmation of justice to its closing denial of injustice.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( 975 ) ( الظلم ظلمات يوم القيامة ) وكما فتح الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive reading, وأشرقت, means the earth became filled and crowded with light, as God fills or covers it with justice.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( وأشرقت ) على البناء للمفعول ، من شرقت بالضوء تشرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الكتاب means the scrolls of deeds; another view identifies it as the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: صحائف الأعمال ، ولكنه أكتفى باسم الجنس ، وقيل : اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الشهداء may be those who testify for and against communities, including angels and righteous people, or martyrs in God’s path.
rows.anchor: الذين يشهدون للأمم وعليهم من الحفظة والأخيار . وقيل : المستشهدون في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After hearing Pharaoh’s plan to kill him, Moses seeks refuge in his Lord, who is also the people’s Lord, inviting them to imitate his appeal and trust in God.
rows.anchor: من حديث قتله : قال لقومه { إنى عذت } بالله الذي هو ربي وربكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase includes Pharaoh and all tyrants while indirectly alluding to Pharaoh, making the rebuke more forceful.
rows.anchor: لتشمل استعاذته فرعون وغيره من الجبابرة ، وليكون على طريقة التعريض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned arrogance is refusal to submit to truth, an especially vile pride that reveals the person’s ignobility and injustice.
rows.anchor: الاستكبار عن الإذعان للحق ، وهو أقبح استكبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tyranny combined with denial of recompense and indifference to consequences completes the causes of hardness and audacity toward God and people, leaving no evil undone.
rows.anchor: لأنه إذا اجتمع في الرجل التجبر والتكذيب بالجزاء وقلة المبالاة بالعاقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عذت and لذت are synonyms.
rows.anchor: وعذت ولذت : أخوان . وقرىء : ( عت )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading assimilates the consonants, yielding عت.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( عت ) بالإدغام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads رجل with a vowelless jīm, as in عضد.
rows.anchor: وقرىء : ( رجل ) بسكون الجيم كما يقال : عضد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account makes the believer a Copt and Pharaoh’s cousin who secretly believed in Moses; another says he was an Israelite. The author favors Pharaoh’s kin, since Israelite believers were not few or weak.
rows.anchor: وكان قبطيا ابن عم لفرعون : آمن بموسى سرا وقيل : كان إسرائيليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His name is given variously as Samʿān, Ḥabīb, or Ḥizbīl; the source also repeats the last form.
rows.anchor: واسمه سمعان أو حبيب وقيل حزبيل أو حزبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may describe the man or attach to يكتم, meaning that he concealed his faith from Pharaoh’s family.
rows.anchor: صفة لرجل . أو صلة ليكتم ، أي : يكتم إيمانه من آل فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites Pharaoh’s own words at 40:25 and the believer’s warning at 40:29 as evidence that the believer addresses his own people with counsel.
rows.anchor: والدليل عليه قول فرعون : { فلما جاءهم بالحق من }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أن يقول means because he says; alternatively, a noun for time is understood, meaning at the moment he said it.
rows.anchor: لأن يقول ، وهذا إنكار منه عظيم

words: أتقتلون رجلا أن يقول ربى الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question forcefully condemns the atrocious killing of an inviolate person for no reason but his truthful confession; the believer also reminds them that the God he names is their Lord too, softening their fury.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنكار منه عظيم وتبكيت شديد ، كأنه قال : أترتكبون الفعلة الشنعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses had brought multiple mighty signs from the one he calls Lord, who is not only his Lord but theirs; the reminder draws them toward acknowledging Him.
rows.anchor: ولكن بينات عدة من عند من نسب إليه الربوبية ، وهو ربكم لا ربه وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are the great clear proofs that the audience had known and witnessed.
rows.anchor: يريد : بالبينات العظيمة التي عهدتموها وشهدتموها

words: وإن يك كاذبا فعليه كذبه وإن يك صادقا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer sets up a dilemma: if Moses lies, the harm of his lie stays with him; if he is truthful, some promised harm will reach them if they attack him.
rows.anchor: ثم أخذهم بالاحتجاج على طريقة التقسيم فقال : لا يخلو من أن يكون كاذبا أو صادقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though a truthful prophet’s full warning must come to pass, the speaker says only some to conciliate Moses’ opponents and sound fair, increasing the chance they will listen and accept his point.
rows.anchor: لأنه احتاج في مقاولة خصوم موسى ومنا كريه إلى أن يلاوصهم ويداريهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By granting only part on the surface, the believer appears to understate Moses’ claim rather than defend him, although his premise that Moses is truthful entails the whole warning; putting the liar first serves the same tact.
rows.anchor: فقد أثبت أنه صادق في جميع ما يعد ، ولكنه أردفه { يصبكم بعض الذى يعدكم }

words: إن الله لا يهدى من هو مسرف كذاب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing claim that God does not guide a profligate liar follows the same tactful, apparently even-handed argument.
rows.anchor: وكذلك قوله : { إن الله * يهدى من هو مسرف كذاب }

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda interprets بعض as meaning all and cites a line by Labīd as evidence; its text is not included in this segment.
rows.anchor: فعن أبي عبيدة أنه فسر البعض بالكل ، وأنشد بيت لبيد :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers of Hell are the attendants charged with torturing its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: لخزنة جهنم } للقوام بتعذيب أهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning Jahannam rather than using a pronoun heightens terror; the name may also derive from جهنام, a deep well, and the poet al-Nābigha was called جهنام for his deep knowledge of poetry.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن جهنم هي أبعد النار قعرا ، من قولهم : بئر جهنام بعيدة القعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worst and most rebellious unbelievers may be in this fire; they deliberately ask its keepers because angels assigned to them might be especially likely to have their prayers answered through their closeness to God.
rows.anchor: وفيها أعنى الكفار وأطغاهم ، فلعل الملائكة الموكلين بعذاب أولئك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers’ question forces proof and rebukes them for having let opportunities to pray and supplicate pass and for neglecting the conditions that make prayers answerable.
rows.anchor: إلزام للحجة وتوبيخ ، وأنهم خلفوا وراءهم أوقات الدعاء والتضرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers say they cannot dare to intercede except for someone who is not an evildoer and when permission is granted, before the final judgment separates the groups.
rows.anchor: فإنا لا نجترىء على ذلك ولا نشفع إلا بشرطين : كون المشفوع له غير ظالم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to ask is an expression of despair, not hope: if a close angel’s prayer goes unheard, a disbeliever’s will fare worse.
rows.anchor: ولكن للدلالة على الخيبة ؛ فإن الملك المقرب إذا لم يسمع دعاؤه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb may mean God responds to believers, with the preposition ل omitted as in 83:3.
rows.anchor: أي يستجيب لهم ، فحذف اللام كما حذف في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may reward believers for obedience and graciously increase their reward, or answer their prayers, grant what they ask, and give them more.
rows.anchor: أي يثيبهم على طاعتهم ويزيدهم على الثواب تفضلا ، أو إذا دعوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the believers are the ones responding: they obey God when He calls them, and He increases their reward from His grace.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الاستجابة : فعلهم ، أي يستجيبون له بالطاعة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr takes the clause as believers’ action: they answer God when He calls them.
rows.anchor: وعن سعيد بن جبير : هذا من فعلهم

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Asked why prayers go unanswered, Ibrāhīm ibn Adham replied that God called people and they failed to answer, citing 10:25 and this verse.
rows.anchor: وعن إبراهيم بن أدهم أنه قيل له : ما بالنا ندعو فلا نجاب ؟
